habitat: Singly or in pairs in the shady understorey of evergreen forest fringes, moist wooded valleys, and riverine and coastal bush.
summary: The Kruger list uses one Bleating Camaroptera, Camaroptera brachyura. Newman’s Green-backed Camaroptera is dark olive-green above and white below, with the tail usually raised. It bleats bzeeeb and, in the breeding season, calls chirrup for long periods. Newman’s Grey-backed Camaroptera has grey upperparts, a creamy-white underside, and the same voice, and replaces the green-backed bird in drier northern and western country. The immature of that form has green upperparts.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^17=131072 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 65536–262144.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

upperparts.pattern: Upperparts entirely dark olive-green. A grey crown occurs in central and southern Mozambique.

viewNotes.note: Small olive-green warbler in the shady understorey, tail often raised. Newman’s grey-backed form is grey above and lives in drier thickets.
The face was not named for the green-backed bird.
The upperwing was not named separately.

calls.description: A goat-like bleat, bzeeeb, and in the breeding season a loud chirrup, chirrup, chirrup. Newman gives the same voice for the grey-backed form. Grade A from Berg-en-Dal, Kruger.

research.note: Status is resident and all twelve months are listed. The stored species is the green-backed Camaroptera brachyura. Newman also describes a grey-backed form with the same voice. That form is not a separate Kruger species in this list, so it is described in the summary and not given its own record.
